title: Set 131

sentences.ko: 내일 등산 가기로 했는데 하루 종일 비가 쏟아진다고 해서 그냥 영화 보러 가기로 했어. 이럴 줄 알았으면 지난주에 새 등산화 안 샀지.
sentences.text: We were supposed to go hiking tomorrow, but they're saying it's going to pour all day, so now we're just going to the movies instead. If I'd known, I wouldn't have bought new boots last week.

alts.text: Hiking's off tomorrow. They're saying it's gonna pour all day, so we're just doing a movie instead. Wish I'd known before I bought new boots last week.
We had planned to go hiking tomorrow, but the forecast is for heavy rain all day, so we will be going to the cinema instead. Had I known, I would not have purchased new boots last week.

sentences.note: **pour** 는 비가 억수같이 쏟아진다는 뜻이에요. **If I'd known, I wouldn't have** 는 알았더라면 안 했을 텐데 하고 지난 일을 아쉬워할 때 쓰는 말이에요.

sentences.ko: 이번엔 다이어트를 목요일까지 버텼어. 근데 누가 회사에 도넛을 사 왔고, 딱 반 개만 먹자고 생각했는데 어떻게 됐을지 알지? 그래서 월요일부터 다시 시작하려고. 지난주 월요일에도 똑같이 말했지만.
sentences.text: I made it till Thursday on my diet this time. Then somebody brought doughnuts into work, and I told myself I'd just have half of one, but you know how that goes. So I'm starting over on Monday, which is exactly what I said last Monday.

alts.text: Got to Thursday on the diet this time. Then someone brought doughnuts to work, and I was like, I'll just have half. Yeah, you know how that goes. So I'm starting over Monday, which is exactly what I said last Monday.

This time I managed to keep to my diet until Thursday. Then a colleague brought doughnuts into the office, and I told myself I would only have half of one, but I am sure you can imagine what happened. I will therefore begin again on Monday, which is precisely what I said last Monday.

sentences.note: **made it till Thursday** 는 목요일까지 버텼다는 뜻이에요. **you know how that goes** 는 뻔하잖아, 어떻게 됐을지 알지 하는 느낌이에요.

sentences.ko: 요즘 머리 자르는 데 얼마 받는지 봤어? 봄에는 25달러였는데 지금은 40달러야. 같은 사람이 똑같이 잘라 주는데. 망치지만 않을 자신 있으면 내가 직접 자르겠다.
sentences.text: Did you see what they're charging for a haircut now? It was twenty five dollars in the spring and now it's forty, and it's the same guy doing the same thing. I'd cut it myself if I thought I wouldn't mess it up.

alts.text: Have you seen haircut prices now? Twenty five bucks in the spring, forty now, and it's the same guy doing the same thing. I'd do it myself if I didn't think I'd screw it up.

Have you noticed how much they are charging for a haircut now? It was twenty five dollars in the spring and it is now forty, for the same barber doing the same work. I would cut it myself if I were confident I would not ruin it.

sentences.note: **what they're charging** 는 가게에서 받는 값이 얼마인지 말할 때 써요. **mess it up** 은 망치다, 엉망으로 만들다라는 뜻이에요.

sentences.ko: 그러니까 그 친구는 간호사인데 밤 근무에 주말 근무도 많아서 시간이 자주 나진 않아. 그래도 말은 진짜 편하게 통해. 좀 직설적이긴 해서 음식이 별로면 그냥 별로라고 말하는데, 너는 오히려 그런 점을 좋아할 것 같아. 네 번호 줘도 돼?
sentences.text: Okay, so she's a nurse and she works nights and a lot of weekends, so she's not free very often, but she's really easy to talk to. She's a little blunt, like if she doesn't like the food she'll just tell you, but I think you'd actually like that about her. Can I give her your number?

alts.text: She works nights as a nurse, plus a lot of weekends, so she's hardly ever free, but she's super easy to talk to. Kinda blunt, like if the food's bad she'll just say so, but I think you'd actually like that. Cool if I give her your number?

She is a nurse who works nights and many weekends, so she is not often available, but she is very easy to talk to. She can be somewhat direct; if she does not care for the food, for example, she will simply tell you, but I believe you would appreciate that about her. Would you mind if I gave her your number?

sentences.note: **easy to talk to** 는 말이 잘 통하는, 대하기 편한 사람을 말해요. **blunt** 는 돌려 말하지 않고 직설적이라는 뜻이에요.
sentences.situation: 친구 소개팅 주선하면서 상대가 어떤 사람인지 설명하기

sentences.ko: 윗집 사람들 매일 밤 가구 옮기나 봐. 11시쯤 되면 누가 소파를 바닥에 질질 끄는 소리가 나거든. 한 번 올라가서 말하려고 했는데 그 집 아저씨가 너무 친절해서 결국 내가 사과하고 왔어. 그래서 이제는 그냥 누워서 듣고만 있어.
sentences.text: The people upstairs must be moving furniture every night, because around eleven it sounds like somebody's dragging a couch across the floor. I went up once to say something, but the guy was so nice that I ended up apologizing to him, so now I just lie there and listen to it.

alts.text: Pretty sure the people upstairs move furniture every night. Around eleven it's like someone's dragging a couch across the floor. Went up once to say something, but he was so nice I ended up saying sorry to him, so now I just lie there and listen.

The neighbours upstairs must be moving furniture every evening, because at around eleven o'clock it sounds as though someone is dragging a sofa across the floor. I went upstairs on one occasion to raise the matter, but the gentleman was so pleasant that I found myself apologizing to him, so now I simply lie there and listen to it.

sentences.note: **must be moving** 은 틀림없이 옮기고 있나 보다 하고 짐작할 때 써요. **ended up apologizing** 은 어쩌다 보니 결국 사과하게 됐다는 뜻이에요.

reviewed: 2번 한국어: told myself 를 '먹자고 했는데'로 옮기면 남에게 말한 것처럼 읽혀서 '먹자고 생각했는데'로 고침
4번 casual: 앞부분 'So she's a nurse' 가 text 의 'Okay, so she's a nurse' 와 겹쳐서 문장 첫머리를 바꿈
5번 casual: 앞부분 'The guys upstairs gotta be moving furniture every night' 가 text 와 거의 같아서 'Pretty sure...'로 시작하게 바꾸고 더 짧게 줄임
5번 한국어: '그 남자가'는 번역투라서 '그 집 아저씨가'로, 끝 문장은 '그냥 누워서 듣고만 있어'로 다듬음
